question: Your Claude Agent SDK agent helps engineers understand legacy systems, and its .mcp.json configures two MCP servers: a database schema server and an issue tracker server. One task requires the agent to inspect the schema of a legacy table and then file an issue about a missing index. A teammate believes that the agent can use only one MCP server per session, so he wants to change the workflow. What should you do?

options.text: Keep one session with both servers configured, because the agent discovers the tools of both servers at connection time and can call either one during the task.
options.reason: The guide states that tools from all configured MCP servers are discovered at connection time and are available to the agent simultaneously.

options.text: Run two separate sessions that each configure only one server, and paste the schema findings from the first session into the prompt of the second session that files the issue.
options.reason: This split is unnecessary. Tools from all configured MCP servers are available at the same time, so one session can do both steps.

options.text: Restart the agent with only the issue tracker server after the schema step, so that tool discovery runs again and exposes the issue tracker tools.
options.reason: The issue tracker tools were already discovered at connection time together with the schema tools, so a restart adds nothing and loses the schema tools.

options.text: Add a system prompt instruction that tells the agent to request activation of the issue tracker server before it calls any tool from that server.
options.reason: No activation step exists. Tools from all configured servers are discovered at connection time and are already available to the agent.
